n: Jerusalem’s people made Ahaziah, Jehoram’s youngest and only surviving son, king, since raiders had killed all the older sons.
Ahaziah reigned only one year. The text says he was forty-two, but 2 Kings says twenty-two, which fits better (his father died at forty). His mother was Athaliah, granddaughter of Omri.

f.g: Likely a copying error; 2 Kings 8:26 and some ancient versions read 22.

n: Ahaziah also followed Ahab’s family ways, because his mother counseled him to do evil. A parent’s influence can lead a child toward God or away.

f.w: his mother was his counsellor to do wickedly

n: After his father’s death, Ahab’s relatives became his advisers — and led him to ruin.
Following their advice, Ahaziah joined Israel’s King Jehoram (Joram), Ahab’s son, in battle against Hazael of Syria at Ramoth-gilead, where Joram was wounded.
Joram went to Jezreel to recover, and Ahaziah (here called Azariah) went to visit him. This visit put him in the path of judgment.
God used this visit to bring about Ahaziah’s downfall: he went out with Joram to meet Jehu, whom the Lord had anointed to wipe out Ahab’s house.
While executing judgment on Ahab’s house, Jehu also killed Judah’s princes and Ahaziah’s nephews who were with him.

f.w: the sons of the brethren of Ahaziah

n: Ahaziah was found hiding, brought to Jehu, and killed. He received a burial only out of respect for his grandfather Jehoshaphat, who sought the Lord wholeheartedly. No one in his family could hold the kingdom.

f.w: who sought the LORD with all his heart

n: When Athaliah learned her son was dead, she seized power and set out to murder the entire royal family of Judah — even her own grandchildren. David’s line came close to ending.

f.g: All the royal descendants who could claim the throne.

n: But Jehoshabeath, Ahaziah’s sister and wife of the priest Jehoiada, rescued the infant Joash and hid him with his nurse in a bedroom. One courageous woman preserved the line through which the Messiah would come.
Joash was hidden in God’s temple for six years while Athaliah ruled. God’s house sheltered the hope of His promise.

f.w: hid in the house of God six years
